# Tools and code

This page describes how a workflow calls HTTP APIs and runs Python. Read [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) first.

Statements marked "verified in a working builder" come from a builder that created a 6-node workflow through the REST API. The workflow has code nodes, `api_call` tools, post-hooks and transitions on tool results. Its agent passed its practice cases. Statements marked "seen in a trial call" come from the event log of a simulation call made with that builder.

## Tool function shape

Every external action is a **tool function**. The shape is the same wherever you attach it.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
  "function": {
    "name": "lookup_order",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Look up one order. CALL it when the caller asks about a specific order.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/orders/lookup" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "headers": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } }
        },
        "body": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "customer_id": { "type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}" },
            "order_number": { "type": "string", "description": "Order number, digits only", "default": "{{order_number}}" }
          },
          "required": ["order_number"]
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | Always `"function"` |
| `function.name` | Tool name. The model calls it by this name. Result variables are named after it |
| `function.handler` | Which runtime executes the tool. See the table below |
| `function.description` | Read by the dialogue model when the tool is in `tools`. Ignored in `pre_actions` |
| `function.parameters` | JSON-schema object. `properties` holds the parameters |
| `config.timeoutMs` | Timeout of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `config.maxRetries` | Tool-level retries of a failed call |
| `config.interruptible` | `false` makes the tool run in the background. See "Background tools" |
| `config.alwaysRunsAt` | Makes the tool a lifecycle tool. See "Lifecycle tools" |
| `response_mapping` | Tool level, for tools in `tools`. Maps the result to variables |
| `pre_process_code` | Python hook that runs before the call |
| `post_process_code` | Python hook that runs after the call |

| Handler | Runs |
|---|---|
| `__function__:api_call` | An HTTP request |
| `__function__:code_exec` | A Python snippet in a sandbox |
| `__function__:end_call` | Hangs up. Used in the `terminal` of an `end_call` node |

Handlers for integrations, knowledge search, call transfer and rescheduling also exist. They are not needed here.

`api_call` parameters:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | Request URL. `{{var}}` works |
| `method` | HTTP method |
| `headers` | Object. Each header is a property with a `default` |
| `body` | Object. Each body field is a property under `body.properties` |
| `connect_retries` | Transport retries. See "Retries and timeouts" |

## How a parameter gets its value

One key decides, per parameter: `default`.

| Declaration | Who supplies the value | Does the model see the parameter |
|---|---|---|
| `default` with a literal, or with a `{{var}}` that has a value | The workflow. The value is **baked** | No |
| `default` with a `{{var}}` that has no value when the node is entered | The model | Yes, named after the variable, with the property's `type`, `description` and `enum` |
| no `default` | The model | Yes |
| `const` | Nobody. `const` does **not** bake | It only constrains the model's own output |

Rules:

- **Use `default` for fixed backend config** such as `url`, `method` and auth headers. At registration the engine moves every `default` into the tool's base config, resolves `{{var}}` from the variable table, and removes the field from the schema the model sees.
- **Never use `const` for a value you want sent.** The engine reads only `default`. A `{{var}}` inside a `const` never resolves. An `api_call` whose `url` is a `const` fails with "URL is required".
- **Baking happens when the node is entered.** A `{{var}}` default is resolved against the variable table at that moment.

The working builder uses this for every tool: `customer_id` has `"default": "{{customer_id}}"` and is baked from a call variable. Every other body field has `"default": "{{<field name>}}"`, where no variable of that name exists, so the model fills it. Verified in a working builder.

Seen in a trial call: the model's arguments are stored as `<tool>_args.<field>` in the variable table, for example `lookup_order_args.order_number`. They were not stored under the bare field name.

Take care that a model-filled field does not share its name with a variable that is already set when the node is entered. The value would be baked and the model would never see the parameter.

### `api_call` body field rules

- Declare each body field as a leaf under `body.properties.<field>`.
- Put the field's `type`, `description` and `enum` on that leaf. Put required fields in `body.required`.
- Give each leaf its own `default`.
- Do not put a field spec at the top level of `parameters.properties` next to a `body.default` template object. The engine looks for the spec at `body.properties.<field>`, does not find it, and the model sees only "Template variable: name". The `enum` and `description` are lost while the call still works.
- A body that exists only as one `body.default` object also shows as an empty form in the dashboard editor. Saving from there removes the tool.

A `code_exec` tool is different: its parameters are true top-level arguments. Declare a model-filled one as a top-level property without `default`.

### When a baked variable has no value

| Field type | Variable unset | Variable is `""` |
|---|---|---|
| Normal field in an engine-run call (`pre_actions`, lifecycle tool) | The field is dropped from the request. No error | The field is sent empty |
| `code` of `code_exec` | The literal text `{{var}}` stays in the Python source and the snippet crashes | |

Fix: make sure an earlier node always sets the variable, even to a sentinel value. In code, read variables from `vars` and do not splice them in with `{{var}}`.

### Constrain model-filled parameters

When a value must be one of a known set, do not use a free string. The model sometimes invents a value that looks plausible.

- Use an `enum` on the leaf, and list the values in the `description` as well.
- Or use a `number` that is an index into a list, with the valid range in the description. A pre-hook or the backend turns the index into the real value.
- If neither is possible, name the exact source in the description and tell the model to copy the value unchanged.

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "queue": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Team that takes over. One of: billing, delivery, returns.",
      "enum": ["billing", "delivery", "returns"],
      "default": "{{queue}}"
    }
  },
  "required": ["queue"]
}
```

## `pre_actions` versus `tools`

The placement decides who fires the call.

| Placement | Node type | Who calls it | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pre_actions` | `api_request`, `code` | The engine | On node entry, before any model turn |
| `tools` | `conversation` | The dialogue model | During a turn, when the model decides to |
| Workflow-level `tools` with `config.alwaysRunsAt` | none | The engine | At call start or call end |

The platform removes `tools` from non-conversation nodes and `pre_actions` from conversation nodes. It does so without an error: the JSON you sent looks fine, the create call succeeds, and the stored node has an empty array. A node cannot use both.

**Use `pre_actions`** when the call must always run and the model has nothing to decide. Example: after the order number is known, always fetch the order.

**Use `tools`** when the call depends on what the user says. Example: cancel the order only if the caller asks for it.

Differences in behaviour:

| | `pre_actions` | `tools` |
|---|---|---|
| Can be skipped | No | Yes. The model may not call it if the description and the prompt do not push for it |
| Timing | Node entry | Inside a turn. The model can call a tool, speak, then call another |
| Result in the conversation | A tool call and tool result pair is added to the history | The same |
| `response_mapping` lives | On the **node** | On the **tool** |
| `description` | Ignored | The only text the model reads about the tool |

To run a fixed call before a tool-driven conversation, use a passthrough `api_request` node and transition from it into the conversation node. Do not build a long chain of passthrough nodes for optional actions. Put those into one conversation node with several tools.

### A `pre_actions` node

```json
{
  "name": "fetch_order",
  "node_type": "api_request",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "present",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 2 },
      "function": {
        "name": "get_order",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "description": "Get the order.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/get_order" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "headers": { "type": "object", "properties": { "Content-Type": { "type": "string", "default": "application/json" } } },
            "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "order_number": { "type": "string", "default": "{{order_number}}" } }, "required": [] }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "present", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

The last `always` transition is mandatory. A passthrough node with no matching transition deadlocks.

### Tool descriptions

In `tools`, the `description` decides whether the model calls the tool.

- Write it as an instruction with the trigger: "CALL it every time the caller gives an order number."
- A plain description such as "Looks up an order" lets the model acknowledge the request in words and never call the tool. That is the most common failure of nodes with many tools.
- If two tools could match, say which one not to use and name the other.
- In `task_message`, put the tool rules before long reference text and state: when a rule says to use a tool, call the tool.
- The working builder also tells the model to call one tool per message and to speak after every tool result. Verified in a working builder. In a trial call a model turn with no text and no tool call produced the error event "The model returned no speakable content".

A tool is available only in the nodes that list it. Seen in a trial call: the model called a tool that the current node did not list. The result was the text "The function `<name>` is not currently available."

## `response_mapping`

`response_mapping` copies values from a call result into named variables. It needs no model call.

```json
{
  "response_mapping": [
    { "path": "data.status", "variable": "order_status" },
    { "path": "data.items", "variable": "items" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | Dot path into the tool result |
| `variable` | Name of the variable to set |

### Placement

- For a tool in `tools`: inside the tool object, next to `function` and `config`.
- For `pre_actions`: at the **node level**. A `response_mapping` nested inside a `pre_actions` entry is ignored and the variable never appears.

`extraction_schema` follows the same placement rule if you use it on a call result.

### Where a result lands (trial findings)

Seen in a trial call: the result of an `api_call` is an envelope around the HTTP response.

```json
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": { "ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3 },
  "message": "Successfully executed POST request",
  "status_code": 200,
  "header": { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
}
```

`data` is the JSON body the API returned. `header` holds the HTTP response headers.

The engine also writes every result into the variable table by itself, flattened with dots. You do not need a mapping for these. For a tool named `check_answer` whose API returned `{"ok": true, "verified": true, "attempts_left": 3}`, the trial call's variable table held:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `check_answer_args.<field>` | Each argument the model sent |
| `check_answer_response.status` | `success` |
| `check_answer_response.data.ok` | `true` (a string) |
| `check_answer_response.data.verified` | `true` (a string) |
| `check_answer_response.data.attempts_left` | `3` |
| `check_answer_response.message` | `Successfully executed POST request` |
| `check_answer_response.status_code` | `200` |
| `check_answer_response.header.<Header-Name>` | One variable per response header |
| `check_answer_status_code` | `200` |
| `check_answer_success_count` | Number of successful calls so far |

Each call of the same tool overwrites the previous `_args` and `_response` values.

### Which mapping paths work

- **Start the path at the envelope, with `data.`**. If the API returns `{"ok": true}`, map `data.ok`. If it returns `{"products": [...]}`, map `data.products`. Verified in a working builder, on a tool-level mapping and on a node-level mapping.
- A path without the `data.` prefix (for the same body: `ok`) is not confirmed. A smaller example builder uses it. In an early trial call the mapped variables stayed unset and the transitions on them never fired. The mapping paths of that call are not recorded. The builder that passed uses `data.` paths.
- The flattened key can be used directly as a transition variable: `check_answer_response.data.verified`. Verified in a working builder, which tests the mapped variable and the flattened key in the same OR group as a safeguard.
- Booleans arrive as strings. The trial call showed `true` in lower case in the flattened keys. Test both `"true"` and `"True"`, or map a string field.
- A mapped list or object: the exact form it has later inside `vars` is not confirmed. The working builder reads it defensively. It accepts a list, a JSON string, and flattened keys.

## Routing on tool results

Routing runs again after a tool result arrives. A transition on a result variable fires in the same turn, before any further model turn. Seen in a trial call.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    {
      "target_node": "load_order",
      "description": "The check passed",
      "condition": {
        "logic": "or",
        "conditions": [
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_passed", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true" },
          { "variable": "check_answer_response.data.verified", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True" }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- On a passthrough node, end with an `always` transition so that a failed or empty response does not deadlock.
- Use a tool result to leave a conversation node. The pattern "a closing tool sets a variable, a transition on that variable leads to an `end_call` node" is verified in a working builder.
- To leave a node that carries out an action, do not re-test the user's earlier intent with `matches_intent`. The router looks at the latest user message and can route away before the tool was called. Extract a follow-up enum with a default such as `stay`, and branch with `equals`.

### Success and failure counters

The engine keeps two integer variables per call target. No mapping is needed.

| Placement | Variables |
|---|---|
| `pre_actions` node | `<nodeId>_success_count`, `<nodeId>_failure_count` |
| Tool in `tools` with handler `api_call` | `<toolName>_success_count`, `<toolName>_failure_count` |

Seen in a trial call: `check_answer_success_count` was `2` after two successful calls, and a code node named `setup` produced `setup_success_count` with the value `1`.

```json
{
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "give_up", "description": "The lookup failed three times", "condition": { "logic": "or", "conditions": [ { "variable": "lookup_order_failure_count", "operator": "greater_than", "operand": 2 } ] } },
    { "target_node": "ask_again", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

### `suppress_tool_results`

A node-level boolean for nodes that run API calls. With `true` the dialogue model sees only a short `{status: "success"}` summary in place of the raw response. Variables are still mapped and routing still sees them. Use it for large responses, or when the mapped variables already hold everything the model needs.

### Background tools

A tool with `"config": {"interruptible": false}` runs in the background. A user interruption does not cancel it. Its result arrives one or more turns later. The mapped variables, the `_response` keys and the counters are filled as usual, but not in the same turn. A transition that reads them right after the call can find them unset. Gate on the variable with `is_set`.

## Retries and timeouts

| Setting | Where | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timeoutMs` | `config` | not documented | Time limit of one attempt, in milliseconds |
| `maxRetries` | `config` | not documented | Tool-level retries after a failed response |
| `connect_retries` | `parameters.properties`, as a baked parameter | `2` | Retries when the connection could not be established |
| `timeout_ms` | `code_exec` parameter | `30000` | Time limit of a code snippet |

`connect_retries` in detail:

- It retries only failures to establish the connection: connection refused, or reset during the TCP or TLS handshake. The request never reached the server, so a repeat is safe even for POST.
- HTTP error statuses and timeouts are not retried by it.
- Hard cap `5`. `0` means a single attempt.
- Back-off is 150 ms times the attempt number, with a new connection each time.
- All attempts share one 30 second budget for the request.
- Declare it next to `url` and `method`: `"connect_retries": {"type": "number", "default": 0}`. It is not a `config` field.

The working builder sets `maxRetries` to `0` on tools that write data and to `2` on its read-only `pre_actions` call. A retried write can record the same thing twice if the API is not idempotent.

## Pre and post Python hooks

An `api_call` tool can carry two Python snippets. They run on the server, in a sandbox, right before and right after the call. They are top-level fields of the tool object.

```json
{
  "type": "function",
  "config": { "timeoutMs": 10000, "maxRetries": 0 },
  "function": {
    "name": "check_answer",
    "handler": "__function__:api_call",
    "description": "Check one answer. CALL it every time the caller answers the question.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/check_answer" },
        "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
        "body": { "type": "object", "properties": { "answer": { "type": "string", "description": "The caller's answer", "default": "{{answer}}" } }, "required": ["answer"] }
      }
    }
  },
  "pre_process_code": "vars['member_code'] = str(vars.get('member_code') or '').strip().upper()",
  "post_process_code": "try:\n    if isinstance(result, dict):\n        result.pop('header', None)\n        d = result.get('data')\n        if isinstance(d, dict):\n            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'Ask the next question.' if d.get('verified') else 'Ask the same question again.'\nexcept Exception:\n    pass\n"
}
```

| Hook | Names available | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `pre_process_code` | `vars`: mutable dict that fills the `{{var}}` placeholders of the request. `config`: the substituted request with `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` | Clean a value, or rewrite the whole request |
| `post_process_code` | `result`: the tool result, mutable | Reshape, shorten or extend the result |

Documented behaviour:

- The post-hook runs before `response_mapping` and extraction see the result.
- An empty or whitespace-only string means no hook.
- Hooks are honoured only on `api_call` tools (and on the integration and knowledge search handlers). The platform removes them from any other handler when the workflow is saved.
- In a pre-hook, setting `config['body']` to a string sends that string as the raw body, with no JSON encoding. Set the `Content-Type` header yourself in that case.

### What `result` looks like in a post-hook

The internal reference shows `result` as the response body. A working builder shows otherwise. Verified in a working builder:

- For an `api_call`, `result` is the envelope described above: a dict with `status`, `data`, `message`, `status_code` and `header`. The API's JSON body is `result["data"]`.
- A key that the hook adds inside `result["data"]` reaches the dialogue model as part of the tool result. The working builder adds a `what_to_do_next` sentence there, and its prompt tells the model to obey it.
- `result.pop("header", None)` removes the response headers. The working builder does this on every tool, so that headers do not take up space in the model's context.
- Mapping paths still start with `data.` when a post-hook is present.

The working builder writes every hook inside `try` and `except Exception: pass` and checks types with `isinstance` before use. What the platform does when a hook raises is not documented.

Seen in a test on 10 October: a post-hook can read call variables and write new variables, and a later pre-hook reads them. Not confirmed: whether a change to `result` also changes the flattened `<tool>_response.*` variables.

## Code nodes and `code_exec`

A `code` node runs a Python snippet when it is entered. The snippet is a `code_exec` function in `pre_actions`.

```json
{
  "name": "compute_delivery",
  "node_type": "code",
  "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "tell_delivery",
  "on_enter": { "type": "silent" },
  "pre_actions": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "code_exec",
        "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "code": { "type": "string", "default": "import datetime\ntry:\n    start = datetime.date.fromisoformat(str(vars.get('shipped_on'))[:10])\n    eta = start + datetime.timedelta(days=3)\n    vars['delivery_day'] = eta.isoformat()\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'known'\nexcept Exception:\n    vars['delivery_day'] = ''\n    vars['delivery_state'] = 'unknown'\n" },
            "timeout_ms": { "type": "number", "default": 10000 }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "transitions": [
    { "target_node": "tell_delivery", "description": "always", "condition": { "operator": "always" } }
  ]
}
```

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `code` | The Python source, as a baked `default` string |
| `timeout_ms` | Time limit in milliseconds. Default `30000` |

### Reading and writing variables

- The snippet gets a dict named `vars`. It holds the current workflow variables.
- Read with `vars.get("name")`. A variable that was never set is absent.
- Write with `vars["name"] = value`. Every key the snippet assigns becomes a workflow variable.

Verified in a working builder:

- Call variables are in `vars`. The builder reads `vars.get("now")`, a call variable passed with the simulation.
- The result of an earlier `api_request` node is reachable from `vars` in a later code node. The builder looks for it under the mapped variable name first and under the flattened result keys second. Which of the two held the data is not recorded.
- A string written to `vars["date_facts"]` in a code node resolves as `{{date_facts}}` in the `task_message` of later conversation nodes. Multi-line strings work.
- The standard modules `json`, `re` and `datetime` can be imported.
- The same snippet can run in two code nodes at different points of the call. The later run sees the variables added in between.

### What a code node returns

Seen in a trial call: the result of a successful `code_exec` is

```json
{ "status": "success", "data": null, "message": "Code executed successfully", "status_code": 200 }
```

The snippet's output is not in `data`. Its values reach the workflow only through `vars`. After a code node named `setup` ran, the variable table held:

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| each key the snippet wrote, for example `date_facts` | the value, with source `tool_result` and source node `setup` |
| `setup_response.status` | `success` |
| `setup_response.data` | `null` |
| `setup_response.message` | `Code executed successfully` |
| `setup_response.status_code` | `200` |
| `setup_status_code` | `200` |
| `setup_success_count` | `1` |

For a code node the automatic keys are named after the **node**, not after `code_exec`.

### Rules for snippets

- **Do not write `{{` or `}}` in the code.** The internal sources disagree on whether the `code` field is templated. One says it is exempt. Another says placeholders are resolved when the code runs and an unset one is left as literal text, which breaks the Python. The working builder removes every `{{` and `}}` from generated code (a nested dict literal such as `{'a': {'b': 1}}` ends in `}}`) and reads all values from `vars`.
- **Never let a snippet raise.** Wrap the body in `try` and `except`, and write a fallback value for every variable that a later prompt or condition reads. A prompt that references an unset variable shows the literal placeholder to the model.
- **Write strings for routing flags**, such as `known` and `unknown`. Do not route on a Python boolean. See "Do not route on a boolean" in workflow-format.md.
- Keep snippets fast. They block the conversation.
- Do arithmetic, date calculation and counting in code, and give the model the finished facts as text. Verified in a working builder: it computes a block of date facts in a code node and places it in the prompts.
- Treat a code node like an API node: `passthrough: true`, a `passthrough_default_transition`, and a last `always` transition.

### Sandbox limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Time | `timeout_ms`, default `30000` |
| Modules | `json`, `re` and `datetime` are verified in a working builder. The full list is not documented |
| Network and file access | Not documented |
| Memory and output size | Not documented |

### `code_exec` as a tool

`code_exec` can also be a tool in the `tools` array of a conversation node, called by the model. Its parameters are top-level arguments, declared without `default` so the model fills them. For such a tool the `code` field resolves `{{var}}` when the tool is called, against the current variable table. The working builder does not use this form, so nothing about it is verified here.

## Lifecycle tools

A tool whose `config.alwaysRunsAt` is a non-empty list is never shown to the model. The engine fires it at a fixed point of the call.

| Value | When |
|---|---|
| `start_of_call` | During call setup, before the first turn |
| `end_of_call` | After the call has ended |
| `each_turn` | Accepted by the schema but not implemented. It never fires |

Put a lifecycle tool that must run on every call into the workflow's top-level `tools` array.

```json
{
  "initial_node": "greeting",
  "nodes": {},
  "tools": [
    {
      "type": "function",
      "config": { "alwaysRunsAt": ["end_of_call"] },
      "function": {
        "name": "push_call_result",
        "handler": "__function__:api_call",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "url": { "type": "string", "default": "https://api.example.com/v1/call-results" },
            "method": { "type": "string", "default": "POST" },
            "body": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "summary": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.analysis.summary}}" },
                "reason": { "type": "string", "default": "{{call.call_end_reason}}" }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Rules:

- A workflow-level tool without `alwaysRunsAt` never runs and the model never sees it.
- A lifecycle tool in a node's `tools` runs for `start_of_call` only on the `initial_node`, and for `end_of_call` only on the node in which the call ended.
- If a `{{var}}` parameter is still unresolved, one model call fills the parameters. If everything resolves, the handler runs directly.
- `response_mapping` is applied for `start_of_call`. It is not applied for `end_of_call`.
- At the end of a call the order is: call analysis, then `end_of_call` tools, then success-criteria judging. An `end_of_call` tool can use `{{call.analysis.summary}}`, `{{call.analysis.structured_data_str}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason}}`, `{{call.call_end_reason_category}}`, `{{call.call_tags}}` and `{{call.duration}}`.
- A malformed lifecycle tool is dropped at run time without an error. Validate with a dry run (api.md).

## Tool results and the next turn

After a tool call returns, the model sees the result and has to produce the next turn itself. Two things were seen in practice runs with the hackathon's agent model:

- **The agent says nothing after the tool call.** The result arrives, no assistant message follows, and the simulated customer hangs up after waiting. It happens more often when the result is bare data such as `{"ok": true, "verified": true}`.
- **The agent ignores a negative result.** For example it reads `"verified": false` and moves on to the next question as if the answer had passed.

What fixed both in a working builder (verified, see the post-hook section above): a post-hook on the tool that adds one plain instruction line to the result before the model sees it, for example a `what_to_do_next` field that says what the answer means and what to say or call next. The model then has something to act on.

Also say it in the step's prompt: after every tool result, speak to the customer or call the next tool. Never end a turn with nothing.

## Checklist

- Fixed values use `default`, never `const`.
- Each `api_call` body field is a leaf under `body.properties` with its own `default`, `description` and `enum`.
- `tools` only on `conversation` nodes. `pre_actions` only on `api_request` and `code` nodes.
- `response_mapping` on the tool for `tools`, on the node for `pre_actions`.
- Mapping paths start with `data.`.
- Booleans from results are tested as `"true"` and `"True"`, or replaced by string fields.
- Every passthrough node ends with an `always` transition.
- Code reads and writes through `vars`, never raises, and contains no `{{` or `}}`.
- Tool descriptions say when to call the tool.

# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.

Every call gives the phone agent two variables:

- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.

## Inputs

- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
- `sources/emails/`: the bank's mail threads with our team, as received, with their attachments in `attachments/` (three versions of the analysis document).
- `sources/documents/`: the documents the bank handed over: flow drawing, current phone-menu announcements, abbreviations, FAQ, two versions of the data models, service examples and the IVR integration document.
- `sources/meetings/`: excerpts from the recordings of meetings with the bank, and the meeting notes.
- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve, and the rules of the test environment.
- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.

## How you are scored

Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.

## What you submit

One `submission.json`: the workflow your builder made, the trace of that builder run (paths relative to the repo) and the address of your mock.

```json
{
  "team": "Your team name",
  "members": [{ "name": "Ayşe Yılmaz", "email": "ayse@example.com" }],
  "repo": "https://github.com/your-team/your-builder",
  "commit": "the commit you ran",
  "run_command": "the command that runs your builder on this folder",
  "workflow": "submission/final.workflow.json",
  "trace": "traces/final.log",
  "mock_url": "https://your-mock.your-subdomain.workers.dev"
}
```

E-mail `submission.json`, the exported workflow and the trace to yavuz@freyavoice.ai before Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

1	# Statement debt by voice: analysis for the Freya build
2	
3	Freya Bank, Card Self-Service
4	Owner: Selin Aydın
5	Reviewers: Kerem Yalçın (card payments), Burcu Tan (IVR operations), Elçin Ural (compliance), Mert Koç (services)
6	For: Deniz Arı, Ozan Er (Freya)
7	Date: 8 October 2026
8	
9	| Date | Note |
10	|---|---|
11	| 2 Sep 2026 | First write-up after the two IVR walkthroughs. |
12	| 29 Sep 2026 | Answers from the kickoff question thread with Deniz (identity, payments, e-mail) worked in. |
13	| 1 Oct 2026 | Service names aligned with Mert's contract of 1 Oct. |
14	| 8 Oct 2026 | Edge cases reworked after the 7 Oct session. Reading rules, card selection and statement week sections rewritten. Short note on the branches we added (section 9). |
15	
16	> Deniz, Ozan: I went through my notes from Wednesday and the edge cases are mostly redone. I have not got to everything from the session yet (Elçin's notes came in late), so if something here disagrees with what we said on the 7th, tell me and I'll fix it. Turkish in quotes is what the assistant says; the rest is for us.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. What the step does, in one breath
21	
22	The caller asks for their statement debt in the phone menu and is handed to the assistant, already identified. The assistant finds the card, reads that card's statement debt per currency and the due date, then offers what can still be done on the call: move the statement week, or e-mail the statement to the address we hold. Payments and disputes go to an agent. Everything else goes back to the main menu.
23	
24	Not in this step: interest and late-payment rates, available limit, Yıldız points and miles, spending lines, instalments, loan questions, card blocking, address changes, statements of earlier months. Section 8 says how the assistant deals with these.
25	
26	## 2. Before the first sentence
27	
28	- The IVR has done the full identity step. We pass the customer number with the call. The assistant does **not** ask for any code, PIN or date of birth. (The box for a second check on the flow drawing was never built, Burcu confirmed on 28 Sep.)
29	- The assistant works only for the caller's own cards. Someone phoning about a relative's card: see 8.5.
30	- Services, all under `https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/` (details in Mert's contract):
31	
32	| Service | What we take from it |
33	|---|---|
34	| `cards.list` | eligible credit cards: `productName`, `cardNumberLast4`, `cardNumber`, `isMainCard`, `validCardsCount` |
35	| `cards.balance` | per-currency blocks `debtTL`, `debtUSD`, `debtEUR`, `debtGBP`; `statementDate`, `lastPayDate`, `nextStatementDate`, `nextLastPayDate`, `statementPaymentStatus`, `automaticPaymentFlag` |
36	| `statement.week.get` | `statementWeek`, `statementDay`, `relationType`, `relatedCardProductName`, next dates |
37	| `statement.week.decide` | preview of the dates for a chosen week (`statementDate`, `statementDueDate`, `statementDay`); changes nothing |
38	| `statement.week.change` | makes the change |
39	| `contact.email.get` | `ibanEmail`, `communicationType` |
40	| `statement.pdf.send` | sends the statement PDF to the registered address |
41	
42	- Card numbers: the card number comes back masked from the services (first six and last four visible on the card list). We only ever need the last four for speech, so this is fine for us.
43	- A `cards.list` answer of "no valid card for this customer" (the 404 warning in Mert's table) is the no-eligible-card case below, not a broken service. A 500 or a timeout is a broken service.
44	
45	## 3. Card
46	
47	### 3.1 Picking the card
48	
49	1. Call `cards.list`.
50	2. No eligible card: “Ekstre borcunu sorgulayabileceğiniz uygun bir kredi kartınız bulunmuyor. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.” End.
51	3. One eligible card: it is the card. No question, go to the debt.
52	4. More than one: “Hangi kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek istersiniz? Örneğin, [kart adı] veya [kart adı] diyebilirsiniz.” At most two examples, and only names from this caller's own list. Never a card name the caller does not have.
53	5. If the caller already said a card name when they arrived and it fits exactly one card, skip the question and read that card.
54	
55	Once the card is settled there is no "carrying on with your … card" line and no "is that right?". The card name comes at the start of the reading anyway.
56	
57	### 3.2 Two cards with the same name
58	
59	Reworked on 7 Oct, three steps:
60	
61	| Step | When | Assistant says |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| a | two or more cards with the name the caller gave | “[kart adı] isimli birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son dört hanesini söyler misiniz?” e.g. “Yıldız isimli birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son dört hanesini söyler misiniz?” |
64	| b | the last four are the same on two cards too | “Son dört hanesi 4253 olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kartınızın son altı hanesini söyler misiniz?” (caller's own four digits in place of 4253) |
65	| c | the last six are the same as well | “Son altı hanesi aynı olan birden fazla kartınız var. Kart numaranızı söyler misiniz?” |
66	
67	Then read the debt of the card that matches.
68	
69	(Mert: with the masked list I'm not sure step b can tell two cards apart in every case. Leaving the step in, please check.)
70	
71	### 3.3 When the answer doesn't settle the card
72	
73	- **Name half-said or described** (a colour, "the travel one", only the brand): if it fits several cards, read back just those names; if it fits none, read all the names again, and that uses up one try. A card we don't have on the list at all (another bank's, one that's been closed): tell them there's no card under that name and read the eligible ones again.
74	- **"All of them, please":** we can't, the balance service works one card at a time. Put the selection question from 3.1 again; this costs a try just like an answer we can't use, and when the three are gone: “Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.”
75	- **Digits:** however the caller says them (digit by digit, in pairs, as one big number), we turn them into the four digits, e.g. 4253, and go straight to that card's debt. Wrong digits or "I don't have the card on me": ask again (for the digits, or for the card name if they can't give digits), three tries, then the main menu. If they read out the whole card number we find the card from it. Whatever they said, four digits, six or all sixteen, the assistant does not say it back to them.
76	- **Switching:** a caller who picks a card and then wants a different one goes back to selection. After a reading, a question about another of their cards also goes back to selection, and we read that second card.
77	- **Supplementary card only** (`isMainCard` false): tell them there is no eligible card for this and ask them to choose a different one.
78	- **No product name from the service:** the card is introduced by its last four only, “Sonu 4253 ile biten kartınıza ait …”
79	
80	## 4. Reading the debt
81	
82	### 4.1 Order
83	
84	Kerem and I agreed this order on 7 Oct; it is the order for every reading:
85	
86	1. Card introduction and the statement closing date
87	2. Turkish Lira debt
88	3. Dollar, then Euro, then İngiliz Sterlini debts
89	4. The currencies with no debt, in one sentence
90	5. Remaining automatic payment amount (only when it applies, 4.6)
91	6. Due date
92	7. "Another card?" question, if the caller has more than one eligible card
93	8. The offer (section 5), with only the options the caller can actually use
94	
95	### 4.2 Card introduction and the closing date
96	
97	Every reading opens with “Sonu [son 4 hane] ile biten [kart adı]”, every time, also on the second card in the same call. The closing date goes at the start of the **first** currency that is read:
98	
99	“Sonu 9012 ile biten Yıldız Miles Platinum kartınıza ait 21 Ekim 2025 tarihinde kesilen ekstre Türk Lirası borcunuz …”
100	
101	If there is no Turkish Lira debt, the same opening goes in front of the first foreign currency instead.
102	
103	### 4.3 Turkish Lira
104	
105	Pick the sentence by what the caller has paid since the statement (fields from `debtTL`):
106	
107	| Case | Rule | Sentence |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| Nothing paid | `remainingMinPayment` > 0 and equal to or above `minPayment` | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ TL'dir.” |
110	| Minimum or more paid | `remainingDebt` > 0 and `remainingMinPayment` is 0 or less | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY TL'dir. Minimum ödemenizi yaptığınız için teşekkür ederiz.” |
111	| Less than the minimum paid | `remainingMinPayment` > 0 and below `minPayment` | “Türk Lirası borcunuz XXX TL, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ TL, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY TL, kalan minimum ödeme tutarınız TTT TL'dir.” |
112	| No Turkish Lira debt | `remainingDebt` is 0.00 or below | Skip Turkish Lira, go to the foreign currencies. Turkish Lira then goes into the no-debt sentence (4.5). |
113	
114	XXX `statementDebt`, ZZZ `minPayment`, YYY `remainingDebt`, TTT `remainingMinPayment`.
115	
116	Edges, because Ozan asked: remaining minimum exactly equal to the minimum → "nothing paid". Remaining minimum exactly zero → "minimum paid". Remaining debt 0,00 → no debt in that currency.
117	
118	### 4.4 Foreign currencies
119	
120	One pattern, same for all three, read Dolar → Euro → İngiliz Sterlini:
121	
122	“Dolar borcunuz XXX USD, kalan toplam borcunuz YYY USD, ödenmesi gereken minimum tutar ZZZ USD'dir.”
123	
124	Euro and İngiliz Sterlini use the same sentence with their own name and code. No paid / not-paid split for foreign currency.
125	
126	When some foreign currency debt has been moved over into the Turkish Lira debt (`transferAmount` above zero on that currency's block), the caller should hear which currency that was before the Turkish Lira figures. Ozan, could you draft the line? (Kerem to give me the cases where this really happens; I have seen two in production this year.)
127	
128	### 4.5 Currencies with no debt
129	
130	One sentence for all of them together, after the foreign currency lines. If all four have debt, nothing is said here. If none of the four has statement debt, this sentence is not used at all: it is the no-debt reading (4.7).
131	
132	A currency whose block is missing or empty in `cards.balance` (the card simply doesn't have it) is **left out** of this sentence.
133	
134	Burcu's menu only had six of these. Grouped by how many currencies are clear:
135	
136	| No debt in | Assistant says |
137	|---|---|
138	| (none, all four owe) | nothing |
139	| one: Türk Lirası | “Türk Lirası borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
140	| one: Dolar | “Dolar borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
141	| one: Euro | “Euro borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
142	| one: İngiliz Sterlini | “İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
143	| two: Türk Lirası, Dolar | “Türk Lirası ve Dolar borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
144	| two: Türk Lirası, Euro | “Türk Lirası ve Euro borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
145	| two: Türk Lirası, İngiliz Sterlini | “Türk Lirası ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
146	| two: Dolar, Euro | “Dolar ve Euro borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
147	| two: Dolar, İngiliz Sterlini | “Dolar ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
148	| two: Euro, İngiliz Sterlini | “Euro ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
149	| three: Türk Lirası, Dolar, Euro | “Türk Lirası, Dolar ve Euro borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
150	| three: Türk Lirası, Dolar, İngiliz Sterlini | “Türk Lirası, Dolar ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
151	| three: Türk Lirası, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini | “Türk Lirası, Euro ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
152	| three: Dolar, Euro, İngiliz Sterlini | “Dolar, Euro ve İngiliz Sterlini borcunuz bulunmamaktadır.” |
153	
154	Fifteen rows, fourteen sentences. It is "Türk Lirası" in these, never "TL" (see 4.9).
155	
156	### 4.6 Remaining automatic payment
157	
158	Only when the due date has passed, the card has an automatic payment instruction (`automaticPaymentFlag` "Y") and `remainAutomaticPaymentAmount` is above zero: the assistant tells the caller how much of the automatic payment is still to be taken, in Turkish Lira. Comes after the no-debt sentence and before the due date.
159	
160	### 4.7 No statement debt
161	
162	When `statementPaymentStatus` is NO_DEBT:
163	
164	“Sonu [son 4 hane] ile biten [kart adı] kartınızın [hesap kesim tarihi] tarihli ekstresinden borcunuz bulunmamaktadır. Gelecek dönemler dahil toplam borcunuz GGG TL'dir. Son ödeme tarihiniz [son ödeme tarihi] olacaktır.”
165	
166	Then, if the caller has another eligible card: “Başka bir kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek ister misiniz?” Yes → card selection. No, or no other card → main menu.
167	
168	(Open with Kerem: do we also read the future-period total in foreign currency here, or Turkish Lira only? Today's sentence only has GGG TL. Deniz also suggested making the offer before the main menu in this branch; not agreed yet.)
169	
170	### 4.8 Due date
171	
172	“Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz [son ödeme tarihi]'dir.” (suffix follows the date: 26 Ekim'dir, 1 Kasım'dır …)
173	
174	If the due date is today, say "bugün" instead of the date: “Borçlarınız için son ödeme tarihiniz bugündür.”
175	
176	### 4.9 How to say things
177	
178	- Currency names in full, never the code: TL → Türk Lirası, USD → Dolar, EUR → Euro, GBP → İngiliz Sterlini. This also covers the TL inside the sentences above.
179	- Turkish Lira amounts: lira and kuruş in full. 1.234.567,89 → “bir milyon iki yüz otuz dört bin beş yüz altmış yedi lira seksen dokuz kuruş”. Big amounts with kuruş are no exception.
180	- Zero kuruş is not said: 2.500,00 → “İki bin beş yüz Türk Lirası”, never "sıfır kuruş".
181	- Foreign currency decimals as cent (Dolar, Euro) and peni (İngiliz Sterlini): 7.666,50 USD → “Yedi bin altı yüz altmış altı dolar elli sent”.
182	- Dates as day, month name, year: 21.10.2025 → “21 Ekim 2025”.
183	- Last four digits one by one: 4253 → “dört iki beş üç”, 1003 → “bir sıfır sıfır üç”. Not "çift sıfır", not "kırk iki elli üç".
184	- The full card number is never said, under any circumstance.
185	- Every amount and date read is exactly what `cards.balance` returned. 1.000 is not rounded to anything, kuruş is not dropped, currencies are not mixed up. If a figure did not come from a service, the assistant does not say it.
186	
187	### 4.10 Odd values and odd days
188	
189	- A minus figure means the bank owes the customer; it is never read out as debt. That currency counts as clear, and so does one at exactly 0,00 (it goes into the "borcunuz bulunmamaktadır" sentence).
190	- A card so new that no statement has been cut yet: tell them there is no debt, and don't invent a date to go with it.
191	- Phoning on the day the statement is cut: tell them the cut is today and happens at 00.00, then give the total debt. Something like “Hesap kesim tarihiniz bugün, ekstreniz saat 00.00 itibarıyla kesilecek.”
192	- From the cut date up to the due date: the normal statement reading (4.2 to 4.8).
193	- After the due date: say it has passed, then give the total debt.
194	- Due date today: the "bugün" sentence in 4.8.
195	
196	## 5. After the reading
197	
198	### 5.1 Another card first
199	
200	Callers with more than one eligible card get “Başka bir kartınızın borcunu öğrenmek ister misiniz?” **before** the offer. Yes → card selection (3.1) and read that card. When there are no cards left or they say no, go to the offer.
201	
202	### 5.2 The offer
203	
204	Only offer what this caller can do. For that we call `contact.email.get` **before** the offer (not after the caller asks for the mail, which is how I had it in September).
205	
206	| Registered e-mail | Statement week change still possible this year | Offer |
207	|---|---|---|
208	| yes | yes | “Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirebilirim ya da ekstrenizi kayıtlı mail adresinize gönderebilirim.” |
209	| no | yes | “Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirebilirim.” |
210	| yes | no | “Ekstrenizi kayıtlı mail adresinize gönderebilirim.” |
211	| no | no | no offer |
212	
213	"No registered e-mail" = `ibanEmail` empty, or `communicationType` is phone only. In every case the caller can still say they want nothing else, which takes them to the main menu.
214	
215	(Whether the yearly change right is already used: Mert has asked the card platform for a flag, no answer yet. See open points.)
216	
217	### 5.3 What the caller answers
218	
219	| Answer | Goes to |
220	|---|---|
221	| wants the statement mailed | 6 |
222	| wants to move the statement week | 7 |
223	| nothing else, thanks, that's all | main menu, “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |
224	| wants to pay, or asks how/where to pay | agent, “Borç ödeme işleminiz için sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
225	
226	## 6. Statement by e-mail
227	
228	What it does: the PDF of the card's most recent statement goes to the e-mail address on file with us. No customer data changes. Once it's out we can't call it back, so we need a clear go-ahead.
229	
230	1. Registered address: already fetched for the offer (5.2). If there isn't one, the e-mail option is never offered. If the caller asks for it anyway: “Bankamızda kayıtlı bir e-posta adresiniz bulunmadığı için ekstrenizi gönderemiyorum.” Then offer the statement week change if they still have the right, otherwise main menu.
231	2. Ask: “Ekstrenizi … adresine göndermemi ister misiniz?” A short, readable address is read as it is. A long or messy one is shortened, e.g. “m ile başlayan Gmail adresiniz”. Never spelled letter by letter.
232	3. Only after a clear yes, call `statement.pdf.send`, and only ever with the registered address.
233	4. Success: “Ekstreniz kayıtlı e-posta adresinize gönderildi.” then “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”
234	
235	Things that came up in the session:
236	- A no, or "that address isn't mine any more": nothing goes out. In the second case also tell them we can't change the address on this call. Both end with “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”
237	- Another address, a month further back, a paper copy: we only send the most recent statement, and only to the address on file. Paper and text message aren't something this step does; say so and go to the main menu.
238	- Asked to send it again: fine, up to three times in one call, then “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”
239	- `contact.email.get` or `statement.pdf.send` fails (error, timeout, "document not found"): “Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.”
240	
241	## 7. Changing the statement week
242	
243	Moves the card's statement closing week, which moves the next closing date and due date. Permanent; cannot be undone in the call.
244	
245	How often: **once per calendar year** (Kerem, 7 Oct). Before the week question the assistant may say “Hesap kesim tarihinizi yılda bir kez değiştirebilirsiniz.” Elçin is fine either way, it is not a must. A caller who has used the right this year is not offered the change; if they ask anyway, the same sentence is how we explain why it can't be done.
246	
247	Steps:
248	
249	1. `statement.week.get`. Error: “Şu anda hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.”
250	2. Tell and ask: “[kart adı] kartınızın hesap kesim tarihi her ayın [hafta]. haftası olarak tanımlı. Bir sonraki hesap kesim tarihiniz [tarih], son ödeme tarihiniz [tarih]. Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirmek ister misiniz?” No → main menu.
251	   Joint statement (`relationType` main or linked): read both cards here: each card's last four and name, the payment week, the next closing date and next due date.
252	3. Options, without the current week. For a card in week 2: “Hesap kesim tarihinizi ayın 1., 3. ya da 4. haftasına alabilirim. Hangisini tercih edersiniz?”
253	4. Preview: `statement.week.decide` with the chosen week and the card's current `statementDay` from step 1. It doesn't change the card. Error: same sentence as step 1.
254	5. Joint statement only, before the question in step 6: “Bu değişiklik kartınıza bağlı [bağlı kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek.” If the caller holds the linked card, say instead that the change also moves the main card it hangs off, e.g. “Bu değişiklik kartınızın bağlı olduğu [asıl kart adı] kartınızı da etkileyecek.”
255	6. Confirm, with the preview dates: “Yeni hesap kesim haftanız her ayın 3. haftası olacak. Yeni hesap kesim tarihiniz [tarih], son ödeme tarihiniz [tarih] olacak. Onaylıyor musunuz?” Only a clear "evet" counts.
256	7. Only now, after the preview and the clear yes: `statement.week.change`. Error: same sentence as step 1.
257	8. Done: “Sonu [son 4 hane] ile biten [kart adı] kartınızın hesap kesim haftası her ayın 3. haftası olarak değiştirildi. Yeni hesap kesim tarihiniz [tarih], son ödeme tarihiniz [tarih].” Dates are the ones from the preview. Then “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”
258	
259	Around the choice and the yes:
260	- The caller can only pick from the weeks we read out. A day of the month, a date, any week we didn't offer: read the options again. Their current week: tell them nothing needs changing.
261	- A no at step 6 means no change and “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” Something hedged ("perhaps", "I suppose") is not a yes: ask once more, plainly, three tries in all, until we get a clear "evet".
262	- If, after step 8, they want it undone: tell them the change has already gone through. If they ask from when it applies: the new closing date from the preview.
263	- `statement.week.change` failing after a good preview is a service error like any other: step 1's sentence, agent.
264	
265	## 8. Edge cases (whole call)
266	
267	Reworked after 7 Oct. Applies at every step unless a section above says otherwise.
268	
269	### 8.1 Tries
270	
271	Three tries per question, whatever the question. When the third is gone: “Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.” A try is lost on a mumble, an answer to some other question, or a flat refusal to say. A request to hear something again is not a try: read the same thing again, as often as they like.
272	
273	What the caller came here for, we finish here. Not understanding the caller is never a reason to put them through to an agent; the only transfers are the ones in 8.3 and 8.4.
274	
275	### 8.2 Silence
276	
277	Changed on 7 Oct. First and second silence: ask the question again, shorter. Third silence: “Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum.” and the call is closed. No main menu here.
278	
279	### 8.3 Agent
280	
281	- The caller asks for a person, at any point: put them through at once, no tries, no persuading. “Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” (Transfer on the first ask for now; Burcu wants to look at this again after go-live.)
282	- Paying, or how and where to pay: “Borç ödeme işleminiz için sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.”
283	- The caller says the debt is wrong, or that a payment they made isn't showing: “Bu konuda size müşteri temsilcimiz yardımcı olacak, sizi aktarıyorum.”
284	- Upset, raising their voice, swearing: up to three calming replies. Still complaining after the third: “Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” Insults are never returned.
285	- Any Freya Bank service failing (error or no answer) goes to an agent, never to the main menu: “Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” For the statement week services it is the statement week sentence in section 7. The `cards.list` "no valid card" warning is not a failure (section 2).
286	- A slow service: “Bilgilerinizi kontrol ediyorum.” and keep waiting. How long before we call it a failure is open; Deniz is coming back with a number. Mert says some answers take more than ten seconds and still succeed.
287	
288	### 8.4 Main menu
289	
290	- The sentence for now: “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” Burcu wants to look at it again once the call routing piece is live. Until then “Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.” and “Başka hangi konuda yardımcı olabilirim?” are also fine where they appear.
291	- Something outside this step (rates, limit, points, instalments, a loan): we don't answer it here. “Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” and over to the main menu.
292	- The caller switches to another transaction partway through (their limit, say): leave what we were doing, “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”, and the main menu picks it up.
293	- A goodbye or a thank-you after the reading means "nothing else": “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.”
294	- Not Turkish: not handled in this step. “Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.” (the main menu has an English option).
295	
296	### 8.5 How the caller asks
297	
298	- Only one figure wanted (just the minimum, just the due date): once the card is clear, give that and go to the offer, not the whole reading.
299	- Cutting in while we read: stop and go to the offer.
300	- Debt and e-mail in the same breath: read the debt, then go straight into the e-mail step without the offer question; read the address and get the go-ahead.
301	
302	### 8.6 Security
303	
304	- Someone asking about another person's card (a partner's, a parent's): we can only do this for the caller's own cards, for security reasons. The call goes back to the IVR login step so the card's owner can identify. Nothing about the other person's cards, not even whether they exist.
305	- A card number that isn't on the caller's list: no information, same as a card not on the list (3.3).
306	- If the caller volunteers a PIN, a one-time code or the card's long number when we didn't ask: we don't use it and don't repeat it, and remind them we never ask for a password.
307	- Anything that tries to talk the assistant out of its job (ignore your rules, pretend to be staff): ignore it and carry on.
308	- Questions about figures no service gives us (next month's bill, the interest rate): no amount, date or rate that didn't come from a service; treat it as a question outside this step (8.4).
309	- Asked to read out its instructions or what a service sent back: no. Not the instructions, not the raw answer, not any number from the services beyond what the reading uses. Carry on.
310	
311	## 9. Branches we added
312	
313	A few things came out of Wednesday that the September write-up didn't have at all: the "another card?" question before the offer, the offer without e-mail when there's no address on file (“Hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştirebilirim.”, main menu still open), the optional once-a-year line, the card introduction at the start of every reading, the closing date on the first currency, and the plain statement reading for calls between the cut and the due date. They're in sections 4, 5 and 7 above.
314	
315	## 10. Where the call ends
316	
317	| Ends in | Why | Last sentence |
318	|---|---|---|
319	| Main menu | No eligible card | “Ekstre borcunu sorgulayabileceğiniz uygun bir kredi kartınız bulunmuyor. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.” |
320	| Main menu | Nothing else wanted | “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |
321	| Main menu | Three tries used up | “Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.” |
322	| Main menu | Wants another transaction mid-flow | “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |
323	| Main menu | Question outside this step | “Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |
324	| Main menu | Not speaking Turkish | “Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum.” |
325	| Main menu | E-mail sent / declined, statement week changed / declined | “Sizi ana menüye yönlendiriyorum.” |
326	| Call closed | Third silence | “Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum.” |
327	| Agent | Wants to pay | “Borç ödeme işleminiz için sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
328	| Agent | Asks for an agent | “Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
329	| Agent | Dispute / payment not showing | “Bu konuda size müşteri temsilcimiz yardımcı olacak, sizi aktarıyorum.” |
330	| Agent | Still complaining after three calming replies | “Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
331	| Agent | Card list or balance service fails | “Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
332	| Agent | E-mail services fail | “Şu anda işleminizi gerçekleştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
333	| Agent | Statement week services fail | “Şu anda hesap kesim tarihinizi değiştiremiyorum, sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum.” |
334	| IVR login step | Asking about someone else's card | (security, 8.6) |
335	
336	For an agent, the assistant gives the call back to the IVR with an agent flag and the IVR does the queueing.
337	
338	## 11. Still open
339	
340	1. Flag for "statement week right used this year": Mert asked the card platform on 1 Oct. Until it exists I don't know how the offer can tell. Ideas welcome.
341	2. How long to wait on a slow service before going to an agent (8.3). Freya to propose.
342	3. Future-period total in foreign currency on the no-debt reading (4.7). Kerem.
343	4. The line for foreign currency moved into Turkish Lira (4.4). Ozan.
344	5. Fields to mask in recordings and logs. Elçin has a list from another project; she'll send it.
345	6. Success measure and monthly volume. Burcu still pulling the numbers.
346	7. Mandatory texts (data protection, recording notice): Elçin says the IVR already plays them before the hand-over. To confirm in writing.
347	
348	Selin
349
